The transcript shows the check **passes today** — the exact condition the "Does it discriminate?" test is meant to catch. With `-W error::DeprecationWarning`, pytest promotes the warning to an error, and yet 13 tests still pass, meaning the warning is not being raised under that flag on this machine. Meanwhile the *second* run (without `-W error`) clearly surfaces 2 warnings. This discrepancy suggests macOS/aarch64 or another environment factor is suppressing the warning when errors are promoted. A check that already passes cannot distinguish "work done" from "nothing changed," so it would grade a no-op implementation as successful. The check needs to run in the same environment/config that actually emits the warning, or use a different mechanism (e.g., capturing warning count) that reliably fails today.
